describes: app-stats.js §23a — section classification, the N02 edge index, and mileage aggregation (the per-category breakdown, ride time, service tiers and 最常乘坐區間). Everything app-stats-render.js does with the result — formatting, Intl collation, DOM — is out of scope.
contract: Coverage is a DEDUPED UNION over N02 edge ids, not an accumulated sum: aggregateMileageStats folds every train's edges into ONE Set and sums idx.km over that Set, so riding a section twice adds it to the total once. Each aggregate case carries summedTrainKm beside it — the accumulating answer — so the two can never be confused for each other. Connector spans (the off-network bridges the solver leaves between matched edges) dedupe separately by span key, are counted nationally, and the mask-0 remainder is reported as unmatchedKm. The ITERATION ORDER of that Set is load-bearing: it is JavaScript insertion order, and a sum of hundreds of thousands of doubles taken in another order is another double, which is why `everything` and `everything-reversed` are both recorded. ride_segment must be EXACTLY true — the feature filter is `!== true`, so 1 and "true" are unridden. Per-train km is the opposite convention on purpose: it accumulates repeats, because it pairs with ride time and ride count in the service-tier rows.

trains.why: Real solver output: 踊り子 down the 東海道線, four station-to-station hops whose vertices are N02 vertices.
Real solver output: あずさ33号 up the 中央線 and onto the 篠ノ井線 — many hops, one of which changes railway.
The SAME ride again under a second train id. The union must not grow; the per-train km must.
The same geometry with every ride_segment false: nothing at all may be collected.
Alternate hops ridden. The flag is per FEATURE, so an unridden hop in the middle leaves a hole rather than shortening the ride.
ride_segment = 1. Truthy, and still unridden: the filter is `!== true`.
ride_segment = "true". Same rule, in the shape a hand-edited JSON file arrives in.
A plain slice of 東海道新幹線 track — the 新幹線 mask, and the baseline the overlap cases are measured against.
A slice that OVERLAPS the previous one (vertices 15–44 against 0–29). The shared edges join the union once; both trains count them in full in their own km.
A slice entirely INSIDE syn_tokaido_full (vertices 5–19): every edge is already in the union, so it adds nothing — and as a section it is contained, which is what dropContainedSections has to notice.
The same slice ridden the other way. Edge keys are direction-independent, so this is the same union — and the same section key, because the endpoints are sorted.

Interpolated midpoints in every N02 edge. A pair-by-pair lookup finds none of these; the anchor-merge walk re-matches each edge when it reaches the far endpoint, so the union must equal syn_tokaido_full's exactly.
Every vertex repeated. The walk skips a hop that goes nowhere rather than treating it as an unmatched bridge.
A short OFF-network detour inside the ride: under MAX_BRIDGE_KM, so it is recorded as one connector span carrying the mask of the edge it reconnects to.
A LONG off-network jump (東海道新幹線 track to 山手線 track): the pending distance passes MAX_BRIDGE_KM, so the span is cut and filed with mask 0 — the unmatchedKm remainder.
MultiLineString: one route with gaps. Each part is walked separately, so the gap between them is not a bridge at all.
from === to. The geometry still joins the union and the train's own km, but no section is recorded — 最常乘坐區間 has nothing to name.
No from/to at all, which is what a hop assembled from geometry alone looks like. Same rule.
One hop crossing two modes — subway track then street tram. The section is filed under whichever mode carries the MOST of its distance, not the OR of every mask it touched.
田沢湖線 track — filed by N02-25 as 在来線 and moved to 新幹線 by the mini-Shinkansen reclassification. The ridden km must follow the corridor override, not the raw N02 code.
One train riding the same stretch there and back in two hops: two SECTIONS with the same sorted key, so the section is counted as two rides and one union contribution.
The same named section measured twice, short first. topRiddenSegments keeps the LONGEST measurement, so a partially-solved repeat must not shrink the recorded length.
A train with no route at all — one unsolvable train must not sink the panel.
Real solver output on the Taiwanese package — a country whose buckets are exclusive, with no JR-style union to record.
Real solver output for the round-island loop: the ride that makes 臺鐵 coverage move.
高鐵 track: Taiwan's hsr bucket, decided by its own institution code 1.
臺鐵 track: CONV-only, which is the mask Taiwan's national-railway toggle reads as "jr".
阿里山林業鐵路: class 31, the 特殊鐵道 slot — a bucket Japan fills with something else entirely.
The 高鐵 ride again: the dedupe rule is country-independent.
Macao is a single-category country: one bucket in activeStatCategories, so a port that hardcodes Japan's six rows has nowhere to put this.
And again, because the dedupe rule does not care how small the network is.

aggregates.label: single
aggregates.why: One real ride: the baseline every dedupe scenario is read against.

aggregates.label: same-entry-listed-twice
aggregates.why: THE case this fixture exists for: the identical entry appears twice in the list. riddenAll must be unchanged from `single`, while the summed per-train km doubles. A port that accumulates instead of folding into a Set fails here and nowhere else.

aggregates.label: same-ride-two-trains
aggregates.why: The same geometry ridden by two trains on two dates — the real shape of a commute.

aggregates.label: overlapping-slices
aggregates.why: Two rides sharing a stretch of track: the union is the outer extent, not the sum.

aggregates.label: contained-slice
aggregates.why: A ride entirely inside another adds nothing to the union at all.

aggregates.label: reversed-repeat
aggregates.why: Direction-independent edge keys: riding back does not discover new track.

aggregates.label: densified-matches-plain
aggregates.why: The densified ride must reach exactly the same union as the plain one.

aggregates.label: bridges
aggregates.why: Both connector-span kinds at once: the short one carries a mask, the long one is unmatchedKm.

aggregates.label: bridges-repeated
aggregates.why: The same spans again. Spans dedupe by span key, so unmatchedKm must not double — the second sighting only ORs its mask into the first.

aggregates.label: unridden-only
aggregates.why: Every ride flag false or merely truthy: an empty union, and zero of everything.

aggregates.label: mini-shinkansen
aggregates.why: Ridden km on a reclassified corridor lands in 新幹線 and NOT in 在來線, while keeping its JR全線 bit.

aggregates.label: repeat-sections
aggregates.why: Sections ridden more than once, which is what drives the 最常乘坐區間 counts and the containment pass.

aggregates.label: everything
aggregates.why: Every ride at once, in declaration order — the union-order case. The Set is iterated in insertion order, so this total depends on the order the trains were walked.

aggregates.label: everything-reversed
aggregates.why: The same rides in the opposite order. The SET is the same; the sum is taken in a different order, so this total may legitimately differ from `everything` in its last bits. Recording both is what makes the order visible instead of accidental.

aggregates.label: tw-repeat
aggregates.why: The same 高鐵 track twice: one union contribution, two per-train sums.

aggregates.label: tw-everything
aggregates.why: Every Taiwanese ride, exercising the country's own category list.

aggregates.label: mo-single
aggregates.why: One ride on a one-category country.

containment.why: A→D ridden more often keeps B→C off the list.
A short section ridden MORE than the long one it sits inside ranks first and keeps the long one as its own entry.
Same edges, different mode: the bucket guard keeps both (sections of different modes never share edges anyway, so this is belt-and-braces).
Three nested sections: containment is tested against everything ALREADY KEPT, not just the previous row.
An empty edge list is never contained (isEdgeSubset refuses it), so an unmatched section survives.

adversarialTrains.why: ride_segment must be exactly true — a truthy 1 does not count.
Nor the string "true".
Fewer than two ridden stops is no ride time at all.
A pass-through inherits its interval, so it is never a ride boundary however it is flagged.
A pass-through between two UNRIDDEN stops stays unridden.
A pass-through at the very START has no previous stopping station, so it falls back to its own flag.
End before start wraps overnight (+24 h) — an itinerary past midnight written without a suffix.
The explicit "+1" spelling, which parseTimeToMinutes already folds in — no second wrap.
25:10 counts up past midnight the jsonspec way.
Departure missing on the first ridden stop falls back to its arrival; arrival missing on the last falls back to its departure.
No usable time at either end is null, not zero.
An unparseable time is null too.
Identical times are a zero-minute ride, not an overnight wrap.
More than two ridden stops: the span is FIRST departure to LAST arrival, ignoring everything between.
新幹線 wins the hsr tier by substring, anywhere in the type.
特急 is the ltd tier — and 通勤特急 matches it by the same substring rule.
A type carrying both words: 新幹線 is tested first.
Missing type falls to other.
Taiwan matches its own vocabulary: 高鐵 is hsr.
…and simplified 高铁 too.
自強 / 太魯閣 / 普悠瑪 / 莒光 are the reserved-seat tier.
Taiwan does not read Japan's words: 特急 is not a Taiwanese tier.
Japan does not read Taiwan's: 自強 is not a Japanese tier.
區間車 falls to Taiwan's other tier.
Only jp and tw have their own vocabulary; every other country falls through to Japan's rules.
